claims.statement: Iron-based superconductors include Fe-pnictogen and Fe-chalcogen layers in several structural families. Their low-energy electronic structure commonly involves several Fe 3d orbitals. Many parent compounds are metallic with coupled magnetic, structural or nematic order; this is a different starting point from a simple single-band cuprate analogy. Kamihara and colleagues' F-doped 1111 material established the early high-temperature platform.
claims.conditions: Retain the structural family, formula convention, excess Fe, doping and pressure. A parent-phase source is not interchangeable with a doped-superconductivity source.
claims.verificationScope: See each source verification label; this ledger does not certify primary findings.

claims.statement: Distinguish 1111, 122, 111 and 11 materials, and treat a single-layer interface separately from a bulk crystal. The K-doped 122 superconductor reported by Rotter and colleagues is not the undoped BaFe2As2 parent. The discovery of superconductivity in FeSe likewise does not imply that its excess-Fe content or electronic structure can be ignored.

claims.statement: A multiband description uses gaps $\Delta_i(\mathbf k)$ on a measured set of bands or orbitals. A candidate s± solution has a relative sign between appropriate Fermi-surface sheets. It is a pairing-model result, not a consequence of the material containing iron. Changes in Fermi surfaces, shallow bands or orbital weights can change which candidate is favored.

claims.statement: The superconductivity-induced neutron response of Ba0.6K0.4Fe2As2 constrains sign-changing pairing models. It does not directly determine the gaps of all 1111, 122, FeSe or interface systems. A synthesis should state the measured wave vector, normal-state spectrum and candidate coherence-factor interpretation.

claims.statement: For an interface, replica bands or a high ARPES gap-closing scale must retain their spectroscopic labels. A reconstructed single-layer Fermi surface may differ substantially from the canonical hole-electron-pocket model. This is why the interface article and the multiband article are separate from a bulk-family temperature comparison.

claims.statement: Several orbitals and strong correlations provide useful organizing language, but they do not establish a universal pairing mechanism. Hund-related mass renormalization is not automatically a larger pairing eigenvalue. FeSe, strongly doped endpoints and interface systems are especially important tests of simple family-wide statements. A strong evidence chain for a candidate gap is different from a unique microscopic verdict.

The most useful database entry is a condition-rich measurement linked to its original compound, not one universal iron-based critical temperature.
